text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Philippine flour millers bought 40,000 tonnes U.S. wheat for July arrival. The firms, including Purefoods Corp, bought a total of 19,000 tonnes western white wheat at $156 to $157 per tonne FOB. The firms also bought 12,000 dark northern spring wheat at $179 to $180 per tonne FOB and 9,000 tonnes dark northern spring wheat with 14 percent protein content at $181 to $182 per tonne FOB.
Other Philippine millers rejected bids for the supply of another 35,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat due to high prices.
WHEAT SALE - South Korea's Daehan Flour Mills Co Ltd bought 21,200 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat from Japanese trader Kanematsu, a company official said on Friday.

The CCC said it bought 35,781 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat under its export program for Armenia. The wheat was purchased from Farmland Inc at $145.24 a tonne, FOB, Galveston. The shipment period was slated for June 30-July 15.
WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC was seeking on June 24 up to 6,750 tonnes of Northern Spring/Dark Northern Spring wheat to Honduras. The shipment period was set for July 10-August 5. Offers were due June 24.

WHEAT TENDERS - Taiwan is expected to tender for up to 66,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat next week, while corn and soybean buyers are sidelined as demand slows down going into the summer season, traders said. The Taiwan Flour Mills Association is expected to place a tender late next week for two 33,000-tonne U.S. wheat shipments, the traders said.

- Pakistan is tendering on June 25 for 500,000 tonnes of optional origin white wheat, July 11-August 10 shipment, a spokesman at the country's U.S. embassy in Washington said. He said the wheat would be either from the United States, Australia or Canada.

WHEAT TENDERS cont'd - The CCC said it was seeking up to 42,000 tonnes of U.S. no.2 or better hard red winter wheat under its export program for Ethiopia. The shipment period was set July 15-July 30. Offers were due on June 26.

- The Cyprus Grain Commission on Wednesday invited tenders for the supply of 12,000 tonnes of soft bread making wheat, a statement from the commission said. Shipment period is scheduled between July 15 and 30, 1997. The tender closing date is Tuesday, June 24.

PALM OIL TENDER - Egypt's official Holding Company for Food Industries was seeking 25,000 tonnes of Malaysian and/or Indonesian palm stearin and palm oil for delivery in August. The deadline for bids was 0900 GMT on June 25. The oils were in the following lots: -- 10,000 tonnes of palm stearin and 15,000 tonnes of palm oil.
CORN TENDER - A group of Philippine feed millers plan to buy between 50,000 and 100,000 tonnes of yellow corn for August arrival, an executive in one of the mills said.
The firms have made price inquiries on U.S. and Chinese yellow corn.

MARKET TALK - Moroccan private and public operators are expected to tap world markets for wheat in mid-July, purchasing an estimated 200,000 tonnes each month, possibly until May 1998, Moroccan grain industry sources said.

... Indications are that China has bought 50,000 tonnes U.S. soybeans for November shipment in the past few days, several U.S. exporters said. But exporters could not confirm rumors that China purchased 125,000 tonnes U.S. soymeal for July/August shipment. "I'm not sure about the meal but about the beans, it did happen," one U.S. exporter said. "I think they did it a couple days ago." He did not have any other details. "It's very possible," a second U.S. exporter said,
